statement:
The edges of a cube are labeled from \(1\) to \(12\) in an arbitrary manner.

a) Show that it is not possible to make the sum of edge-labels at each vertex the same.

b) Show that if one of the labels is changed to \(13\), we can label the edges so that all eight vertices have the same sum.
Given any convex polygon, show that there exist three consecutive vertices such that the polygon lies inside the circle passing through them.

We are given \(n\) objects of identical appearance but different masses, and a balance that can compare any two objects (one object per pan). How many weighings are necessary and sufficient to find both the heaviest and the lightest object?
Let \(a, b > 0\) be reals such that \(a^3 = a + 1\) and \(b^6 = b + 3a\). Show that \(a > b\).

A \textit{super-integer} is an infinite sequence of decimal digits \(\ldots d_n \ldots d_2 d_1\). Given two super-integers \(\ldots c_n \ldots c_2 c_1\) and \(\ldots d_n \ldots d_2 d_1\), their product \(\ldots p_n \ldots p_2 p_1\) is defined by taking \(p_n \ldots p_2 p_1\) to be the last \(n\) digits of the ordinary product \(c_n \ldots c_2 c_1 \times d_n \ldots d_2 d_1\). Can we find two nonzero super-integers whose product is the zero super-integer (all digits zero)?
A triangle has semiperimeter \(s\), circumradius \(R\), and inradius \(r\). Show that it is right-angled if and only if \(2R = s - r\).
